description: Needs a rent.dev account: sign in when your client offers it, or call rent_signup first. For someone who runs a machine, their own or a VPS rented elsewhere, and wants to sell its compute; to get a machine to use, rent a sandbox instead, with rent_create_sandbox on /mcp or POST /v1/sandboxes over REST. Makes claim tokens for new nodes, one per node, each valid for 10 minutes and shown only in this answer. `lines` holds the exact shell line for each token: run it on the machine and the node kit sets the machine up, claims the node, links it and reports each step. The token reaches the kit on stdin, never as a process argument. On a host the claim comes after the install, and a first install can outlast the token: when the line ends with `claim_invalid`, call this tool again and run the same line with the new token. `payout` registers the USDC address every node of this enrolment is paid to; without it the nodes are not paid until one is set with rent_supply_update_node. Ask the user for the address; never make one up. Each node is paid once a day, in USDC, to the address registered on that node; a node without an address is not paid and its releasable earnings wait until one is registered. A payout cannot be reversed, and a payout made is never sent again to another address. A refusal carries `retryable`, `owner_action_required` and `next`; run `next.command` after `next.after_s` seconds, on a driver machine through npx and with its driver file, as rent_supply_guide says.

ask.description: What you ask per hour. Customers pay this plus rent.dev's take.

cpu_usd_per_vcpu_hour.description: USD per vCPU-hour, a decimal string: "0.01".

memory_usd_per_gib_hour.description: USD per GiB-hour, a decimal string: "0.002".

slots.description: Sandboxes the node runs at once.

count.description: Nodes to enrol: one claim token each. Default 1.

payout.description: Where this node's payouts go. Each node is paid once a day, in USDC, to the address registered on that node; a node without an address is not paid and its releasable earnings wait until one is registered. A payout cannot be reversed, and a payout made is never sent again to another address.

address.description: The USDC address payouts go to: 0x and 40 hex digits, lowercase or with a correct EIP-55 checksum, never the zero address.

network.description: CAIP-2 network of the address, e.g. `eip155:8453`. Leave it out for the payout network; any other is refused.

region.description: A generic region label such as `us-central` or `eu-central`, never a vendor's.

wire.description: `e2b`: a Linux host where the node kit installs the sandbox stack. `rent`: a driver file you write for your own platform.

name: rent_supply_enroll

lines.description: One entry per claim token: the exact shell line with that token in it.

driver.description: Run beside your driver file, for wire `rent`; put its path in.

host.description: Run on the host, for wire `e2b`.
